lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Gerald, it's Marcus. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the walking?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 1 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you watch TV in bed?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I got home late every day this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Work took over this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd do it if the day had a few more hours.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have more energy when I go to bed earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the pain gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the pain made this week harder, you still got 1 days in, and your plan is to be in bed by 10 on 5 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Marcus. Bye!

flags.reason: Repeats the same phone advice verbatim after participant voiced 'I don't really see the point'; ignores sustain talk and pushes advice.
Summary says pain made the week harder and quotes a 5-night bedtime plan the participant never stated; misrepresents the conversation.
Introduces 'pain' as a barrier though participant only mentioned heat and work; the reference is unsupported.

score.summary: Gerald showed real change talk around his daughter's reminders, his fear of recurrence, and planning the night before, but Marcus repeated unsolicited advice after Gerald said he didn't see the point. The closing summary also misstated pain and a bedtime plan, which weakens the collaborative goal-setting.
strengths: Line 16: well-timed reflection of Gerald's ability when he plans the night before, with affirmation at line 17.
Line 19 and 26: asks permission before sharing ideas, respecting autonomy.
Line 30: open question about what went well drew out change talk at lines 31 and 33.
Line 38: clear follow-up plan with midweek text and two-week check-in.
coaching_tips: Line 28: after 'I don't really see the point' (line 25), explore the sustain talk with a reflection or open question instead of repeating the phone advice.
Line 34 and 36: stick to what Gerald actually said; he never mentioned pain, so ask about barriers in his words.
Line 36: let Gerald state his own plan in the summary rather than supplying '5 nights' yourself; ask 'What feels doable this week?'
Line 3 and 5: name and explore feelings (e.g., the heat, fear of recurrence) before moving to goals, and set an agenda at the start.
